# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory, loads the raw SRA metadata, and optionally merges supplement tables.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
# EDIT HERE: change project_id for each study
project_id <- "PRJEB11419"

base_dir <- "D:/metadata_collect"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE)

# (3) OPTIONAL: If extra metadata (e.g., Table.x or supplemental materials) are available from the article, you may need to merge the file with initial_meta manually. Below is example code for merging. Depending on the specific case of each study, you can customize the code as needed.
# supp_table <- read.csv("supplemental_table.csv", header = TRUE)
# initial_meta <- left_join(initial_meta, supp_table, by = merge_col_name)
```

# Step 2: Data Overview

First, you need to get an overview of the data, which includes two steps: reading the article and reading the initial metadata. This step is very IMPORTANT!

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# (1) Article overview:
# Title: "American Gut: an Open Platform for Citizen Science Microbiome Research"
# Authors: McDonald D, Hyde E, et al. (mSystems, 2018, Vol 3, e00031-18)
# Study: American Gut Project (AGP) - citizen science microbiome study
# Participants: >10,000 citizen scientists; primary regions: US (n=7,860), UK (n=2,518), Australia (n=321), plus 42 other countries
# Sample types: gut (fecal/dry swab), oral (saliva), skin
# Sequencing: 16S rRNA V4 region, Illumina MiSeq
# Primers: 515F-806R
# This project aggregates samples from multiple cohorts worldwide via the Qiita platform.

# (2) IMPORTANT: MUST go through each column of initial_meta
head(initial_meta, 10)

# IMPORTANT: Check the unique values in the column of interest or query column.
# Organism column: unique values and counts
# human gut metagenome (35213), human oral metagenome (2755), human skin metagenome (1630),
# human nasopharyngeal metagenome (325), human vaginal metagenome (159),
# human metagenome (79), human eye metagenome (54), gut metagenome (16),
# food metagenome (10), feces metagenome (3), human blood metagenome (2), metagenome (4142)
table(initial_meta$Organism)

# sex column: female, male, Not provided, unspecified, other, LabControl test, Not applicable, not collected, not provided
table(initial_meta$sex)

# age_cat column: 30s, 50s, 40s, 60s, 20s, 70+, child, teen, baby, Unspecified, Not provided, LabControl test, not collected
table(initial_meta$age_cat)

# country_residence column: United States, United Kingdom, Mexico, Australia, Canada, Germany, Ireland, etc.
table(initial_meta$country_residence)

# Instrument column: Illumina MiSeq (dominant), Illumina NovaSeq 6000, Illumina HiSeq 2500, Illumina HiSeq 4000
table(initial_meta$Instrument)

# ReleaseDate column: multiple dates from 2015 to 2025
table(initial_meta$ReleaseDate)

# target_subfragment (exp) column: V4 (34711), V9 (565), ITS1/2 (472), empty (8640)
table(initial_meta$target_subfragment..exp.)

# pcr_primers (exp) column: multiple primer pairs
table(initial_meta$pcr_primers..exp.)
```

# Step 3: Filtering to Oral Samples Only

We keep only human oral metagenome samples and remove controls, non-human, non-16S, and non-oral samples.

```{r}
# (1) Filter: keep only human oral metagenome
initial_meta <- initial_meta[initial_meta$Organism == "human oral metagenome", ]

# (2) Remove control samples: "LabControl test" keyword in sex column
control_column <- "sex"
control_keywords <- c("LabControl test")

# (3) Remove non-bacterial 16S: remove ITS, 18S rRNA, and empty target_gene
non_16s_column <- "target_gene..exp."
non_16s_keywords <- c("ITS", "18S", "^$")

n_samples_before <- nrow(initial_meta)

# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0 && control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta)) {
  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, initial_meta[[control_column]])
} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples_before)
}

# Non-bacterial 16S evaluation
if (length(non_16s_keywords) > 0 && non_16s_column %in% colnames(initial_meta)) {
  non_16s_pattern <- paste(non_16s_keywords, collapse = "|")
  is_non_16s <- grepl(non_16s_pattern, initial_meta[[non_16s_column]])
} else {
  is_non_16s <- rep(FALSE, n_samples_before)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_16s
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Oral samples before filtering:", n_samples_before, "\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-16S samples:", sum(is_non_16s), "\n")
cat("Total removed:", sum(samples_to_remove), "\n")
cat("Remaining oral samples:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.
The uniform metadata should include the following columns:
1. **bioproject**: Project ID from SRA or other database
   e.g. `PRJNA1234`, `CNP1234`, 'OEP1234', 'qiita_1234'
2. **sample_id**: SRA sample/run ID. Unique id for each sample!
   e.g. `DRR1234567`, `ERR1234567` and `SRR1234567`. If no such column exists, can use column like sample_name.
3. **subject_id**: subject id for each person if available.
   e.g. `patient_01`, `Host_03_before`, `subject12`
4. **age**: Age of the subject if available.
   e.g. `35`, `42` | not `adult`, `chilren`
5. **age_info**: If the age is not explicitly stated but approximate age range information is available, mark it in this column.
   e.g., `18-55`, `children`, `infant`, `elder`
6. **bmi**: Body Mass Index if available.
   e.g. `22.5`, `18.9` | not `normal`, `overweight`
7. **sex**: Sex of the subject.
   Mandatory to write as M/F | not `female`, `woman`
8. **sequencing_region**: Targeted 16S rRNA region.
   e.g. `V3-V4`, `V4`
9. **platform**: Sequencing platform.
   e.g. `Illumina MiSeq`, `454 GS FLX Titanium`, `Ion Torrent`
10. **country**: Country of sample origin.
    e.g. `China`, `Japan` | not city name like `Beijing`
11. **site**: Sampling site. For oral and gut sites, specify the exact sites as detailed as possible. For example, if it is known to be supragingival plaque, do not record it as 'dental plaque', unless the original text provides only a vague description.
    e.g. `saliva`, `tongue coating` | not broad term like `oral`
12. **site_group**: only accepts one of following three values: 'oral', 'gut', or 'other'.
13. **public_time**: Data release date.
    e.g. `2021-06-22` | not `June 2021`
14. **pcr_primers**: PCR primers used.
    e.g. `515F-806R`, `27F-338R` | not primer sequences
15. **title**: Title of the associated publication.
16. **disease_study**: Whether the study involves disease samples. If it's not clear, can record as NA. Only three values accepted: 'yes', 'no' or NA
17. **status**: Disease status for each sample if available, else record as NA. Only accept following abbreviations, Write full names for all other diseases.
    HC: healthy control
    CD: Crohn's disease
    CRC: colorectal cancer
    COPD: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
    HIV: human immunodeficiency virus
    ICU: intensive care unit
    OSCC: oral squamous cell carcinoma
    RA: rheumatoid arthritis
    UC: ulcerative colitis
18. **matched_samples**: Whether the subject has matched samples. Only accept 'yes' or 'no'.
19. **is_time_series**: Whether the study is a time series study. Only accept 'yes' or 'no'.

```{r}
# Extract columns from initial_meta as follows:
# (1) No modification needed -> extract directly.
# (2) Modification needed -> create a new column with the prefix raw_ and mark the original column as "pending".
# (3) Need to find or determine based on the article.
#
# Source annotations:
#   bioproject: CSV column BioProject
#   sample_id: CSV column Run
#   subject_id: CSV column Sample_name (Qiita sample ID)
#   age: derived from CSV column Birth_Year (approximate)
#   age_info: CSV column age_cat (self-reported age range: 20s, 30s, 70+, etc.)
#   bmi: calculated from CSV columns height_cm and weight_kg (pending, resolved in Step 5)
#   sex: derived from CSV column sex (recoded: female->F, male->M)
#   sequencing_region: CSV column target_subfragment..exp.
#   platform: CSV column Instrument
#   country: CSV column country_residence
#   site: "oral" (filtered in Step 3)
#   site_group: "oral" (derived from site)
#   public_time: CSV column ReleaseDate
#   pcr_primers: CSV column pcr_primers..exp., used directly
#   title: paper title (McDonald et al., mSystems 2018)
#   disease_study: "yes" (cohort includes participants with various diseases)
#   status: derived from survey columns with fixed answer pattern (pending, resolved in Step 5)
#   matched_samples: pending (determined later by subject_id)
#   is_time_series: "no" (cross-sectional study, paper Results)

metadata <- data.frame(
  bioproject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  sample_id = initial_meta$Run,
  subject_id = initial_meta$Sample_name,
  age = NA_character_,
  age_info = initial_meta$age_cat,
  raw_height_cm = initial_meta$height_cm,
  raw_weight_kg = initial_meta$weight_kg,
  bmi = "pending",
  raw_sex = initial_meta$sex,
  sex = "pending",
  sequencing_region = initial_meta$target_subfragment..exp.,
  platform = initial_meta$Instrument,
  country = initial_meta$country_residence,
  site = "oral",
  site_group = "oral",
  public_time = initial_meta$ReleaseDate,
  pcr_primers = initial_meta$pcr_primers..exp.,
  title = "American Gut: an Open Platform for Citizen Science Microbiome Research",
  disease_study = "yes",
  status = "pending",
  matched_samples = "pending",
  is_time_series = "no",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) resolve disease status from survey columns.

```{r}
# (1) Handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix.
# Recode sex: "female" -> "F", "male" -> "M"; others -> NA
# Source: CSV column sex, direct recoding
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(sex = case_when(
    raw_sex == "female" ~ "F",
    raw_sex == "male" ~ "M",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Compute approximate age from Birth_Year
# Source: CSV column Birth_Year; calculated as 2018 - Birth_Year (year of paper publication)
# Converted to numeric; non-numeric values become NA
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(age = ifelse(
    initial_meta$Birth_Year != "" & !is.na(initial_meta$Birth_Year) & initial_meta$Birth_Year != "Not provided" & initial_meta$Birth_Year != "Unspecified" & initial_meta$Birth_Year != "not provided",
    as.character(as.numeric(2018) - as.numeric(as.character(initial_meta$Birth_Year))),
    NA_character_
  ))

# Calculate BMI from height_cm and weight_kg
# Source: CSV columns height_cm (cm) and weight_kg (kg)
# No unit conversion needed; column names indicate cm/kg already
# Filter empty, "Not provided", non-numeric, and extreme outliers
compute_bmi <- function(height_raw, weight_raw) {
  h <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(height_raw)))
  w <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(weight_raw)))

  # Filter invalid and extreme outliers
  h <- ifelse(is.na(h) | h < 50 | h > 250, NA_real_, h)
  w <- ifelse(is.na(w) | w < 10 | w > 400, NA_real_, w)

  # Calculate BMI: kg / (m)^2
  h_m <- h / 100
  bmi <- w / (h_m ^ 2)
  bmi <- ifelse(is.na(bmi) | bmi < 10 | bmi > 80, NA_real_, bmi)

  return(round(bmi, 1))
}

metadata$bmi <- as.character(compute_bmi(metadata$raw_height_cm, metadata$raw_weight_kg))
```

```{r}
# (2) Resolve disease status from survey columns.
# Only use specific, well-defined diseases:
#   IBD (ibs column) + ibd_diagnosis_refined -> CD / UC
#   cdiff -> C.diff
#   Diabetes -> Diabetes
# All other disease columns are too broad to classify precisely.
# HC: all 3 confirmed negative
# NA: any disease column is unknown (not fully answered)
#
# Source columns:
#   ibs, ibd_diagnosis_refined, cdiff, Diabetes
#
# Answer format for all 3 columns:
#   YES: "Diagnosed by a medical professional (doctor, physician assistant)",
#     "Self-diagnosed", "Diagnosed by an alternative medicine practitioner"
#   NO: "I do not have this condition" (case-insensitive)
#   NA: "", "Not provided", "not provided", "not collected", "Unspecified"

has_disease <- function(val) {
  if (is.na(val)) return(NA)
  val_trimmed <- trimws(val)
  if (val_trimmed == "") return(NA)
  if (tolower(val_trimmed) == "i do not have this condition") return(FALSE)
  if (val_trimmed == "Not provided") return(NA)
  if (val_trimmed == "not provided") return(NA)
  if (val_trimmed == "not collected") return(NA)
  if (val_trimmed == "Unspecified") return(NA)
  return(TRUE)
}

resolve_status <- function(row_idx) {
  diseases <- c()
  has_unknown <- FALSE

  # IBD: use ibs column for yes/no, ibd_diagnosis_refined for CD/UC split
  ibd_result <- has_disease(initial_meta$ibs[row_idx])
  if (is.na(ibd_result)) {
    has_unknown <- TRUE
  } else if (ibd_result) {
    ibd_refined <- initial_meta$ibd_diagnosis_refined[row_idx]
    if (grepl("Crohn", ibd_refined, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      diseases <- c(diseases, "CD")
    } else if (grepl("Ulcerative colitis", ibd_refined, ignore.case = TRUE) ||
               grepl("Microcolitis", ibd_refined, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      diseases <- c(diseases, "UC")
    } else {
      diseases <- c(diseases, "IBD")
    }
  }

  # C.diff
  cdiff_result <- has_disease(initial_meta$cdiff[row_idx])
  if (is.na(cdiff_result)) {
    has_unknown <- TRUE
  } else if (cdiff_result) {
    diseases <- c(diseases, "C.diff")
  }

  # Diabetes
  diabetes_result <- has_disease(initial_meta$Diabetes[row_idx])
  if (is.na(diabetes_result)) {
    has_unknown <- TRUE
  } else if (diabetes_result) {
    diseases <- c(diseases, "Diabetes")
  }

  # If any disease confirmed, return disease name(s)
  if (length(diseases) > 0) {
    return(paste(diseases, collapse = "+"))
  }
  # If all confirmed negative -> HC
  if (!has_unknown) {
    return("HC")
  }
  # Otherwise some are unknown -> NA
  return(NA_character_)
}

metadata$status <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(metadata)), resolve_status)

```

```{r}
# (3) Filling the 'matched_samples' column
# editing matched_samples, just run.
metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(
  ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length) > 1,
  "yes",
  "no"
)
```

```{r}
# (4) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
# Function to check if a column contains "pending"
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

# Check for any pending value
any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
# Select columns for visualization, just run
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

# Generate and arrange plots
plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$age_info,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$pcr_primers,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata.csv` file.

```{r}
# Reorder the data frame
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), everything())

# save metadata
# head(metadata)
write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE)
```
